claims.text: Controlled thermal pre-oxidation of boride-based components forms a thin, coherent, adherent Al2O3 surface layer.
Pre-oxidation improves the molten-aluminum corrosion resistance of boride-based components relative to untreated components.
Boride-based components are prone to rapid degradation in molten aluminum.
The pre-oxidation treatment can produce a uniform alumina layer on the component surface.
The alumina layer acts as a physical and chemical barrier between the boride substrate and molten aluminum.
The alumina barrier reduces interdiffusion between molten aluminum and the boride component.
The alumina barrier reduces reactive dissolution of the boride component in molten aluminum.
Reduced interdiffusion and reactive dissolution inhibit molten-aluminum corrosion.
Pre-oxidized components will have lower weight loss than untreated controls after molten-aluminum exposure.
Pre-oxidized components will preserve structural integrity better than untreated controls after molten-aluminum exposure.
The intervention remains effective while the alumina layer remains intact and adherent at the molten-aluminum exposure temperature.
Thermal cycling or mechanical stress may disrupt or degrade the protective alumina layer.
